sales_hooks: Huawei Ascend 910C is creating a self-contained China AI supply chain — NVIDIA export controls are accelerating China's domestic HBM alternatives (CXMT), which threatens global HBM supplier market share in China.

Huawei CloudMatrix 384 cluster benchmarks are improving rapidly — if China AI self-sufficiency succeeds, ~35% of global AI compute demand could be served domestically, reducing HBM export addressable market.
China hyperscalers (ByteDance, Baidu, Alibaba) are dual-sourcing: NVIDIA (where licenses allow) + Huawei Ascend — understanding this split is critical for memory supplier sales into China.
Huawei's domestic memory reliance on CXMT creates a vulnerability: CXMT's HBM-equivalent is 1-2 generations behind SK Hynix/Samsung — this gap is a sales opportunity if export controls relax.

competitive_position.vs_nvidia: Performance gap closing; export controls are Huawei's market tailwind
competitive_position.vs_domestic_asic: Huawei competes with Biren, Cambricon; Huawei has strongest software ecosystem (MindSpore)
competitive_position.risk_factors: US entity list restrictions; TSMC access denied; reliant on SMIC N+2 (7nm equivalent)

scm_engagement.scm_role: China's leading AI chip designer and AI server vendor, operating a fully domestic supply chain (SMIC foundry + CXMT HBM) to circumvent US export controls. Huawei's Ascend GPU is the primary alternative to NVIDIA in China, and its Atlas server platform is the primary AI training server for Chinese hyperscalers.

lead_time.description: Huawei Ascend chip → tokens served ≈ 16 months inside China. Longer than NVIDIA because SMIC N+2 yield is lower (more scrapped wafers = longer to fill order), CXMT HBM supply is constrained, and MindSpore software stack requires more porting.
lead_time.bottleneck: SMIC N+2 yield rate (~60% vs TSMC N5 ~80%) — doubles effective lead time for same volume
